name: Kemps
description: Kemps (also known as Kent or Cash) is a fast-paced partnership card game where teams try to collect four-of-a-kind and signal their partner to call 'Kemps!' The game involves secret signals, quick card exchanges, and trying to intercept opponents' signals.

history.origins: Kemps is a relatively modern American card game that emerged in the 20th century. The exact origin is unclear, but it has been popular in the United States since at least the mid-1900s. The game is also known as Kent in some regions.
timeline: Mid-20th century: Game emerges in USA
Late 20th century: Spreads as popular party game
Present day: Played at parties and gatherings
Modern era: Available in app form
history.cultural: Kemps is popular as a party game and among groups of friends. The secret signal aspect makes it a social and often humorous game. It is commonly played at summer camps, college dorms, and casual gatherings.
history.evolution: The game evolved from older four-of-a-kind collection games. The unique elements are the secret signals between partners and the simultaneous card exchange from the center layout, creating a game of observation and deception.

rules.objective: Be the first team to score a predetermined number of points (usually 5) by successfully calling 'Kemps' when your partner has four-of-a-kind, or by calling 'Stop Kemps' when an opponent is about to call.
rules.gameplay:
1. Partners secretly agree on a signal (gesture, word, or movement) to indicate they have four-of-a-kind
2. Each player receives 4 cards
3. Four cards are placed face-up in the center
4. When play begins, players simultaneously exchange cards with the center
5. Players can swap any number of cards (1-for-1, 2-for-2, etc.)
6. No turns - it's a free-for-all
7. Players try to collect four-of-a-kind in their hand
8. When a player gets four-of-a-kind, they give their secret signal to their partner
9. The partner calls 'Kemps!' to score a point
10. If 'Kemps' is correct, the team scores
11. If 'Kemps' is wrong (false alarm), the team loses a point
12. Opponents can call 'Stop Kemps' or 'Counter-Kemps' if they think someone is signaling
13. If a 'Stop Kemps' is correct, the calling team scores; if wrong, they lose a point
keyRules: Partners must agree on a secret signal before play
Signals can be gestures, sounds, or movements - but not words with meaning
Players must maintain exactly 4 cards in hand
The center must always have exactly 4 cards
Card swapping is simultaneous - no turns
First to touch a center card gets it if there's a dispute
'Kemps' must be called by the partner, not the player with four-of-a-kind
'Stop Kemps' can be called at any time

strategy.basic: Choose a subtle signal that's not obvious to opponents. Watch your partner closely for the signal. Try to collect four-of-a-kind quickly.
strategy.intermediate: Use multiple signals to confuse opponents. Watch opponents for their signals. Fake signals to draw out opponents' 'Stop Kemps' calls. Coordinate with partner on which cards to collect.
strategy.advanced: Sophisticated signaling systems with multiple meanings. Reading opponents' body language. Strategic use of false signals. Optimal card selection based on visible cards.
tips: Choose a signal that's natural and not too obvious
Don't stare at your partner - opponents will notice
Watch opponents' eyes to see what they're watching
Fake a signal when you don't have four-of-a-kind to draw out opponents
Have backup signals in case opponents guess your main one
Don't call 'Kemps' too quickly - make sure you saw the signal
Watch for opponents' tells when they're close to four-of-a-kind
